s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with palpitations and transient loss of consciousness
salient_findings: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring recorded polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode
Coronary angiography showed 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: QTc of 403 milliseconds and history of syncope

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode

shortlist.label: Coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of syncope and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of syncope and palpitations, possible obstructive component

raw.rationale: The patient experienced syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis, and 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring recorded polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode, which is consistent with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc of 403 milliseconds is within normal limits, making Long QT syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Coronary artery disease
rejected.why: While coronary angiography showed significant stenosis, the patient's symptoms and Holter monitoring results suggest an arrhythmic cause of syncope rather than a cardiac ischemic event.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of right ventricular dysfunction or structural abnormalities on echocardiography or other imaging studies.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's echocardiogram showed a normal left ventricular ejection fraction and no mention of hypertrophy, making this diagnosis unlikely.
